• 4309092 “Environment contains chemical hazards”, 4309405 “Environment contains physical hazards”, 4173945 “Environment contains biological hazards” and 4308614 “Environment contains traffic hazards” describe characteristics of a setting, not a person’s contact/exposure event, and each covers only a subset of hazards, making them either contextually incorrect or too narrow.
• 4305831 “Exposure to potentially harmful entity” is an event but is broader than the source because it includes harms unrelated to the physical environment (e.g., infectious contacts, ingested drugs). Hence it over-generalizes beyond the specified ‘physical environment’ hazards.
• Other candidates (e.g., occupational-specific or accident-specific exposures) introduce additional context (occupational, accidental) not present in the source.

As none of the candidate concepts is clinically and semantically equivalent without being broader or narrower, no exact match is available.
